conbody.p: Use the LONG_POLLING_TIME_MS query option to control how long, in milliseconds, Impala waits on the server side for a query to complete when a client requests the status of the query.

After submitting a query, a client polls the query status until the query reaches the 'FINISHED' state or fails. A query in the 'FINISHED' state means that the rows are available to be fetched, or, for statements that do not return rows, that the statement has completed. When this query option is set to a value greater than 0, status requests (GetOperationStatus for HiveServer2 clients) wait until the query reaches the 'FINISHED' or the error state, or until the specified time elapses, whichever comes first. The request then returns the current state of the query, which is not necessarily a final state.

Waiting on the server side lets the client learn that the query finished as soon as it happens, instead of after the sleep between two client-side polls. This reduces the latency of short queries. impala-shell shortens its sleep between polls by the time that the status request took.
When this query option is set to 0, status requests return the current state of the query immediately, without waiting.
The option only affects status requests. Requests that submit a query, such as ExecuteStatement, do not wait for the query to finish.
conbody.note: The default value was changed to 250 starting from . In earlier releases the default was 0, so status requests returned immediately. To restore the previous behavior, set LONG_POLLING_TIME_MS=0.
